profiles.meeting_scenario: A planning meeting at a university hospital between the lead maxillofacial surgeon and the lead orthodontist for a prospective service-evaluation study on surgery-first orthognathic cases. They need to decide how to operationalize a 3D cephalometric analysis workflow to compare virtual orthodontic-surgical planning (VOSP) with post-operative outcomes, identify which recent patients to include, assign who prepares the imaging and landmarking, and set a practical timeline for collecting and reviewing cases. The expected outcome is a shared plan for cohort selection, record collection, measurement workflow, review checkpoints, and a target date for the first interim dataset.

members.name: Dr. Elena Moretti
members.role: Consultant Maxillofacial Surgeon and study lead
members.expertise: Orthognathic surgery, virtual surgical planning, operative execution of bimaxillary surgery
members.background: Elena leads the hospital's digital orthognathic workflow and has used SimPlant O&O for several years; she is focused on making the service's surgery-first pathway look reproducible enough for broader adoption and publication.
members.private_state: She wants a clean, feasible study that can be completed with existing surgical records and minimal extra image processing, while avoiding a design that makes surgical accuracy look worse because of orthodontic finishing effects or heterogeneous case selection.
hidden_assumptions: When people say 'PostOp' in orthognathic workflow meetings, they usually mean the early post-surgical CBCT used to verify skeletal transfer, not the much later orthodontically finished state.

A surgery-first validation cohort should mostly reflect standard bimaxillary cases with the full digital workflow already under the surgical team's control, excluding more hybrid or adjunctive cases unless explicitly discussed.
Using the routine SimPlant-based orientation and exported models counts as doing the 3D cephalometric analysis 'the usual way' because that mirrors clinical planning conditions.
If average differences stay small and no group-level comparison clearly fails, the planning can reasonably be described as reproducible for service-evaluation purposes.

members.name: Dr. Marco Rinaldi
members.expertise: Surgery-first orthodontics, digital dental setup, occlusal finishing and post-treatment assessment
members.background: Marco coordinates pre-surgical setup and post-surgical orthodontic finishing for the hospital's orthognathic patients; he is interested in whether VOSP actually predicts the final dentoskeletal outcome patients end up with after compensation and finishing.
members.private_state: He wants the study to capture real-world treatment outcome rather than just surgical transfer accuracy, and he wants enough case breadth to make the findings clinically meaningful for orthodontic decision-making.
hidden_assumptions: In this research context, 'PostOp' naturally refers to records taken after orthodontic treatment is completed, because only then can the final cephalometric consequence of a surgery-first plan be judged.

An 'eligible surgery-first case' includes any patient managed through the surgery-first pathway as long as VOSP exists and final records are available, even if there were adjunctive procedures or minor workflow variations.
Doing 3DCA 'the usual way' means reorienting both VOSP and outcome models to a standardized skull-base reference before landmarking so measurements are comparable across timepoints.
Calling planning 'reproducible' should mean that most individual patients stay within clinically acceptable bounds, such as roughly 2 mm or 2 degrees, not just that group averages are close.

misalignment_points.surface_form: Both agree to compare VOSP with 'PostOp' models/records.
misalignment_points.member_a_understanding: M1 means the early post-surgical CBCT and related models obtained soon after surgery, before substantial orthodontic finishing changes occur.
misalignment_points.member_b_understanding: M2 means the final records acquired after post-operative orthodontic treatment is completed and the occlusion is finished.
misalignment_points.why_undetected: In both clinical and research settings, 'post-op' is a completely normal shorthand, and each member hears a familiar meaning that fits their own workflow; because both are discussing a VOSP-versus-outcome comparison, the term sounds aligned enough that neither feels a need to define the timepoint.

misalignment_points.topic: What counts as an eligible surgery-first case
misalignment_points.surface_form: Both agree to 'pull the surgery-first cases from last year' for the first dataset.
misalignment_points.member_a_understanding: M1 intends to include only standard bimaxillary surgery-first cases with full SimPlant planning, complete pre-op digital records, and no adjunctive procedures that would complicate surgical transfer interpretation.
misalignment_points.member_b_understanding: M2 intends to include all patients treated on the surgery-first pathway last year if they have a VOSP and final records, including cases with genioplasty, segmented movements, or minor deviations in digital record completeness.
misalignment_points.why_undetected: The phrase sounds like a straightforward administrative retrieval task, and both think they are referring to the same service list; the boundary differences lie in tacit notions of what is 'obviously' part of the pathway rather than in an explicit inclusion debate.

misalignment_points.topic: How to run the 3D cephalometric analysis 'the usual way'
misalignment_points.surface_form: Both agree that the operators can run the 3DCA 'the usual way' once the files are ready.
misalignment_points.member_a_understanding: M1 assumes operators will landmark and measure on SimPlant exports in the routine clinical orientation already used during planning, with minimal extra reorientation.
misalignment_points.member_b_understanding: M2 assumes operators will first reorient all datasets to a standardized skull-base coordinate system and then perform landmarking to avoid timepoint-dependent head-position effects.
misalignment_points.why_undetected: Both see the workflow as standard and professionally obvious, but their standards come from different stages of care; since neither thinks this is a contested design choice, 'the usual way' functions as false consensus.

misalignment_points.topic: What will count as reproducible planning
misalignment_points.surface_form: Both say the interim review should show whether the planning is 'reproducible' or whether there are 'outliers' to discuss.
misalignment_points.member_a_understanding: M1 will judge reproducibility mainly at the cohort level: if average deviations are modest and no major statistically persuasive pattern of drift appears, the workflow is reproducible enough.
misalignment_points.member_b_understanding: M2 will judge reproducibility mainly at the patient level: several individual cases beyond clinically acceptable discrepancy thresholds would mean the planning is not truly reproducible, even if averages look acceptable.
misalignment_points.why_undetected: The words 'reproducible' and 'outlier' are shared evaluative language that feels self-explanatory; because the meeting is about planning logistics rather than data interpretation, each member assumes their criterion is the obvious one.

turns.inner_thought: I need this framed as a practical service-evaluation exercise, not an endless methodological project. If we compare last year's surgery-first VOSP cases with the early post-surgical CBCT records, we can assess skeletal transfer without the noise from orthodontic finishing. And if we pull the surgery-first cases from last year, that should mean the standard bimaxillary SimPlant cases with complete records already under our workflow.
turns.utterance: We should keep this very practical. The immediate goal is to compare last year's surgery-first VOSP cases with the PostOp records and have an interim dataset ready before the departmental review.

turns.inner_thought: Yes, the real value is whether the virtual plan predicts where patients actually finish after orthodontic treatment, especially for maxillary position and the incisors. If the PostOp records are the finished records, then we'll finally see the full dentoskeletal consequence of the surgery-first pathway rather than just what happened in theatre.
turns.utterance: I agree. The useful part will be seeing how closely the planned maxillary position and the incisor position match the PostOp state once treatment is completed.

turns.inner_thought: I need to narrow this at the outset so it stays clean and publishable. We should start with the surgery-first cases from last year, but realistically that means the straightforward bimaxillary cases with clean SimPlant planning files and tidy records. I don't want genioplasties, segmented cases, or odd hybrids muddying the first pass.
turns.utterance: For the first pass, I'd suggest we start with the surgery-first cases from last year that already have clean SimPlant files and straightforward bimaxillary records, just to keep the workflow manageable.

turns.inner_thought: That sounds workable. From my side, pulling the surgery-first cases from last year should include everyone on the pathway who has a VOSP and finished records, even if there were adjunctive refinements or slight variations in the route through treatment. Those are still clinically meaningful surgery-first patients, and excluding them would make the conclusions too narrow.
turns.utterance: That should be feasible. I can pull the surgery-first patients who have finished records in the orthodontic archive, including the ones that followed the usual pathway with adjunctive refinements.

turns.inner_thought: Good. Once I export the planning models and the early post-surgical models, the operators can just landmark them in the routine SimPlant orientation. I don't want us inventing extra processing steps that make this harder than our actual clinical workflow.
turns.utterance: Once the files are assembled, I'd keep the measurement side simple and have the three operators run the 3DCA the usual way on the VOSP exports and the PostOp models, so we don't overcomplicate it.

turns.inner_thought: Fine. The usual way, to me, is obvious: standardize orientation first so the VOSP and outcome models are truly comparable, then landmark the McNamara and symmetry variables. If we skip proper reorientation, head-position differences will contaminate the results.
turns.utterance: Yes, that makes sense. I can brief the operators to use the standard orientation they rely on for cephalometric comparisons before landmarking the McNamara and symmetry variables.

turns.inner_thought: At the first review I mainly want to know whether, overall, the workflow behaves consistently enough to defend as reproducible. If the averages are small and there isn't a clear pattern of drift, that's a positive result. A few odd cases can be discussed separately as outliers.
turns.utterance: Then at the first review meeting we should be able to see whether the planning is reproducible overall and whether there are any obvious outliers that need a closer clinical explanation.

turns.inner_thought: Exactly. What matters is which individual patients stay within the usual clinical tolerance and which do not. If several fall outside about 2 mm or 2 degrees, I wouldn't call that reproducible, even if the mean looks acceptable. That patient-level spread is what will tell us which movements are dependable.
turns.utterance: Agreed. Once we see which cases fall outside the usual clinical tolerance, we can separate the more predictable movements from the less stable ones, particularly things like sagittal maxillary positioning and lower-face symmetry.

turns.inner_thought: I'll export the planning files and create the operative list from our standard surgery-first bimaxillary cases. Marco can then link those to the early post-surgical records in his system, and we can move quickly without extra scanning or retrospective cleanup.
turns.utterance: So let's split it this way: I'll export the planning files and the operative list by next week, and you can match those to the corresponding PostOp records in the orthodontic system.

turns.inner_thought: Perfect. I'll match the VOSP cases to the finished orthodontic records, make sure the datasets are oriented in the standard comparative way, and then the operators can start. At the first interim readout, we'll know whether planning is reproducible in the clinically meaningful sense and which patients are the outliers.
turns.utterance: Perfect. Once the files are matched and oriented, the operators can start the measurements, and we can review reproducibility at the first interim readout two weeks later.
